findings.description: The security group allows SSH (port 22) access from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the management port to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks against the instance.

The security group allows HTTP (port 80) access from 0.0.0.0/0. While this may be intended for a public web server, combined with the unrestricted SSH rule it indicates an overly permissive security posture with no CIDR restriction at all.

AWS access key and secret access key are hardcoded in plaintext inside the instance user_data script, exposing long-lived IAM credentials to anyone with access to the instance metadata, console, or Terraform state.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, leaving data at rest unencrypted and readable if the underlying storage or snapshots are exposed.
The EBS snapshot inherits from an unencrypted volume, so the snapshot itself is unencrypted, risking exposure of sensitive disk data if the snapshot is shared or leaked.
The S3 bucket used to store VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration, leaving potentially sensitive network traffic metadata unencrypted at rest.

findings.issue_category: missing public access block / bucket policy
findings.description: The S3 bucket has no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, and force_destroy is enabled, which combined with no access controls could allow unauthorized access to sensitive flow log data.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to all instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure of instances to the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to all instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure of instances to the internet.
